verdict.first_step_1: Set up a test feed at a 1:5:5 ratio in a marked jar (either side-by-side or boosted with whole wheat/rye) and observe movement within 6 to 12 hours.
verdict.first_step_2: Run a side-by-side feed at a 1:1:1 ratio in marked jars, measure temperature, and track whether it doubles across three feeding cycles.
verdict.reason: Reply 2 correctly uses a standard 1:1:1 feeding ratio and insists on tracking doubling over three cycles, whereas Reply 1 prescribes an aggressive 1:5:5 dilution evaluated after only a single cycle.

first:**  
If this were my problem, I would act on **Reply 2** first. 

While Reply 1 nicely articulates that timing alone does not prove causation, its practical recommendation is flawed: subjecting an already sluggish starter to an aggressive 1:5:5 dilution (20 g starter to 100 g flour and water) and judging it after only 6 hours of a single cycle risks misdiagnosing a slow culture as dead. Reply 2 aligns with the correct troubleshooting protocol by maintaining a gentle, standard 1:1:1 feeding ratio in a marked jar, tracking doubling, and explicitly noting that observations must span three feeding cycles because a single cycle is noise.
